newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges Turkey to seek alternatives to Iran gas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Turkey to seek alternatives to Iran gas.

text.p: U.S. officials Thursday reiterated Washington's concerns about Turkey buying natural gas from Iran and urged it to seek other alternatives.

While Turkey considered its $23 billion, 23-year natural gas contract with Iran as a way to diversify its supply sources, acting U.S. Energy Secretary Charles Curtis said Turkey was buying into "false security."

He and oil company officials said Turkey should look at natural gas supplies from the Caspian Sea, Yemen, Qatar, Egypt, Nigeria, Algeria, and Abu Dhabi to bolster imports which currently come from Russia.

"We're simply reminding you of the advantage of working with more secure suppliers," U.S. Commerce Department counselor Jan Kalicki said at a conference sponsored by the Turkish-U.S. Business Council, American Turkish Council, and American Friends of Turkey.

Turkey is expected to need some 60 billion cubic meters a year of natural gas by 2010, more than half of which is expected to fuel soaring power generation demand, according to U.S. and Turkish executives.

The main advantage of natural gas from Iran is that it would be delivered by pipeline, which was 30 percent cheaper than liquefied natural gas (LNG) delivered by tanker, said Mustafa Murathan, general manager of Turkish state pipeline company Botas.
Energy Minister Recai Kutan said Wednesday construction of a pipeline to carry Iranian gas would begin in late March or early April.
Washington disapproved of the Turkish deal with Iran, saying it would counteract efforts to isolate Iran and cut off funding for its alleged support of terrorism and nuclear weapons acquisition.
